title: Keep focus visible
summary: Focus marks the control that receives keyboard input.
introduction: Focus marks the control that receives keyboard input. Your task: Use Tab to reach the button, then activate it.
learningObjectives: Use Tab to reach the button, then activate it.
Explain the example for keep focus visible

blocks.text: Focus marks the control that receives keyboard input. The focus method can move the typing cursor to an input when that helps the reader.
The HTML examples are complete small page parts. Use this site's HTML Run button. Put the script after the elements it uses so those elements already exist.

blocks.code:
<label for="search">Find a book</label><input id="search"><button id="start">Go to search</button>
<script>
  document.querySelector("#start").addEventListener("click", () => {
    document.querySelector("#search").focus();
  });
</script>
blocks.title: Keep focus visible

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A label's `for` value names the input id. That connection lets the label describe and focus the intended field.
`addEventListener` waits for the named event before calling the function you pass to it.
`focus()` moves keyboard focus to a control. Use it for a clear task, not for every ordinary page update.

blocks.text: Clicking Go to search moves focus into the search field. You can then type.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not move focus on every page update. Unexpected jumps make a page hard to use.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Use Tab to reach the button, then activate it.
